Text: A net of whispers cast over the docks. Someone high up is hauling it in.
Aelius kept a list. Argonian names, for the Oculatus.
Truth can wear two faces, Listener. Your task is not to make one disappear.
Aelius was kind to them. That was true.
That knot? Fisherman's hitch, marsh style. My lads use a bowline. Theirs use that.
Whoever it is, they work after dark. Nobody's that brave at noon.
I hear the harbor has been giving back bodies.
Four since the thaw. All Nords. The names were familiar from complaints. I recorded those too.
The fifth came up this morning. East pier. Bring a strong stomach and a sharper question.
They say less when a Nord is holding the ledger. Ask them yourself. If they stay to answer.
And the Argonians? What do they say?
No bruising on the hands. He did not fight the water. He fought someone before it took him.
What was different about this body?
Dockhands, mostly. Men who lost cargo, teeth, or both. Haldor Frost-Knuckle's name appears often.
Who complained about the men who drowned?
Names come after the count. If the count is wrong, the names do not help.
You count the dead before you ask who they were.
Because the killer knows rope. Or wants us to think he does. Either way, the knot was tied in a hurry.
Why use a fisherman's knot for a killing?
Haldor. He said they were settling a debt. Haldor calls every beating a debt.
Who was the last man seen with him?
There. You see the ledger now, warm-blood. It has teeth even when the ink is dry.
You ask about drowned Nords in the Argonian quarter? Brave, or stupid. Maybe both, stranger.
What do you know about the drowned men?
Coin remembers better than I do. The knots, stranger. Look at the knots.
(Bribe) Maybe this helps you remember.
Then look at the knots, stranger. Not every hand in this harbor learned them in Skyrim.
(Persuade) I'm not a guard. I'm the last one who'd report this.
Everyone is the last one until they aren't. Go away.
Back to work, lizard, before I feed you your own tail.
What, no hissing tonight? Good. You're learning.
Something pulled me under! Guards! Guards!
What... something's got my leg! Help!
We'll take him. There were complaints, yes. Dock disputes, we thought. Your payment will be recorded.
We called it dock trouble. That was convenient. Trouble does not need a report signed against it.
A dark elf in my Hollow. Is the whole city walking through my door tonight?
Aelius paid us fair. He learned our names. You ask me to drown the only warm-blood here who ever...
You call this a test. The warm-blood gets kindness, and I get a blade.
Good evening, Sings-Beneath-Ice. You drown beautifully. You also drown loudly.
He kills from hatred, Listener. Hatred is loud. The family is quiet.
Aelius, the harbor clerk. He dies before dawn. By your hand, Sings.
I ask you to kill without hating. If you cannot, you are a grudge with a knife.
Kindness is not innocence. A hand may soothe and still keep a list.
You will learn what he kept. First, decide what you are keeping inside yourself.
I will be in Dawnstar. Do not keep me waiting, Listener. Do not keep him waiting either.
A pool in the dark. You know how to tempt an Argonian.
Come to Dawnstar. There is a pool there that needs a shadow.
I will take the road south. May your water stay calm, Listener.
Leave Windhelm and do not come back.
Then do it quickly. I would do the same for you.
The family has no room for you.
You lead me into the dark only to hand me to the light? Coward.
The Jarl's guards will want a word with you.
Sings? You are late. Is something wrong at the docks?
At this hour? You are shaking. Here, take my cloak. It is freezing out.
You have been quiet all week. Did someone at the docks threaten you?
I know. I write complaints until the ink dries, then I write another.
Not often enough. But a closed door is still better than a grave.
Nothing is wrong, Aelius. Walk with me to the water.
Everyone threatens someone. Most only call it work.
And did the ink ever open a door?
Close your eyes. The water is not cold after the first breath.
Clean water is a story. I can choose what I put into it next.
You can condemn the list without pretending the killing was clean.
No. That is why your knife feels heavier when you speak his name.
Then Aelius is not on that list.
Let it notice. The water keeps what it takes. Mostly.
Five bodies before tonight. The city will notice the next.
I knew the name before I knew the face. Veezara's family. I thought the Emperor's dogs had drowned you all.
In the Marsh, they might have taken me young and taught me the Shadowscale's work. Here, I was a dockhand.
They beat us with the same hands they pray with. I only introduced those hands to the water.
The Dark Brotherhood.
Family. A word the Nords never had for us.
He works late. He always works late. That is the kind of man he is.
Do this, and I will judge you for more than your anger.
Hands. Boots. Doors that closed before I reached them. A body learns its list.
You remember every hand that hurt you.
You smell of the Void, stranger. Not a guard, then. Something worse.
Haldor. You pulled him out. Why? He would not have pulled you.
No. If it must be done, it will be done by the one who owes him.
If you will not, I will.
His desk is locked. Aelius never locked anything.
He wrote our names down. Every one. For the Emperor's dogs.
So I was right to hate, and wrong about whom.
I agreed to kill him before I knew. His betrayal cannot change that.
He wrote our names to protect a city that never learned them.
So, Listener. Do I follow you into the dark, or does the water have one more guest?
What else is there to kill for? Coin? That is how Nords think.
You kill well. Do you kill for anything but hate?
A leash. Yes. I have felt it tighten every night.
(Persuade) Hate is a leash. Kill him, and you will never wear it again.
The water has no fear. It only remembers what is given to it.
You protected them by making the water afraid of them.
A name for the dark. A place where scales were not a crime. I have not decided if that is enough.
What did Veezara's family give you?
Then you watched justice. It is quieter than the priests promise.
Someone who watched what happened at the docks.
Windhelm's harbor has been giving back bodies. Four this season. The guards blame the cold.
The cold does not tie knots.
Find out who ties them. Then find out whether he can tie one without hating the neck inside it.
He came. Good. He will read Veezara's name on the wall every night.
Gone south, then. I hope he finds something worth staying for.
...Sithis takes them all eventually.
Handed to the Jarl. An interesting choice for a Listener.
